To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new method for nanoengineered YBCO thin film growth, which combines substrate decoration, quasi multilayers, and a secondary phase nanoinclusion in a YBCO target.

the combined use of substrate decoration, quasi multilayers and a BZO-doped target gave the highest pinning properties reported so far for YBCO thin films, with the absolute maximum in pinning occurring in the a-b plane for fields higher than 1 T.

a 4% BaZrO$_{3}$-doped target, combined with Ag nanodots grown by PLD on a Ag-coated MgO substrate, gave the best results in terms of Ic-w at 77 K, and that the highest Ic values were obtained for a 5.5 μm thick BZO-doped film grown on 5.8 nm Ag dots.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fabrication of YBCO thin films with enhanced critical current densities, by means of a combination of three different approaches: substrate decoration with Ag nanoparticles, the use of a BZO-doped target, and the fabrication of Ag/YBCO quasi-multilayers.
the development of a new technique for nanoengineering of the pinning landscape in YBCO thin films, by combining substrate decoration with Ag nanodots and the use of a BZO-doped target.
the study of the pinning landscape in YBCO films with nanoengineered pinners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of all the three techniques (substrate decoration, quasi-multl-layers, and secondary phase nanoinclusion in targets) is very promising, and should be further investigated.
this new approach, combining three previously reported techniques, has given the best results so far, with a clear second peak in Ic-w at 77.5 K, and the highest Ic values at 77.4 K.
the best results in terms of Ic-w and Ic-c, were obtained with the 5.8 nm Ag nanodots/YBCO/BZO trilayer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best Ic-w values were obtained in samples with Ag nano-dots on top of a BZO-doped quasi-multilayer, with the Ag nano-dots being the most effective for out-of-plane pinning, while the BZO-doped layer being most effective for in-plane pinning, with the quasi-multilayer being most effective in the intermediate field range.
, in order to obtain high Ic-w, it is not sufficient to use a BZO-doped target, nor to decorate the substrate with nanodots, but it is necessary to combine both approaches.
, in terms of Ic, we have obtained a 3-fold improvement over our previous results for Ag nanodots and a 2-fold improvement for BZO-doped targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the first time to our knowledge, we have demonstrated the feasibility of combining three approaches for the fabrication of pinning centers in YBCO thin films, and the potential of the resulting pinning centers for high-field applications.

, in the case of the 5.8 nm Ag/YBCO/BZO trilayer, the combination of Ag nano-dots and BZO-doped target gives a much better pinning performance than the sum of individual performances, as shown by comparison with a 5.5 nm BZO/YBCO/BZRO trilayer.
a combination of three different approaches for nanoengineered YBCO films can be used to achieve a very smooth change from out-of-plane to the in-plane pinning, with high values of Jc-w.
